title: Usher — 1 Library & Catalog
description: Eleven panels, every one SQL against the canonical database. PRD 10's first principle: most of what is worth knowing about a media catalog is not a metric. There is deliberately no Prometheus target on this dashboard.

panels.title: Titles by enrichment state
panels.description: titles.enrichment_state. The whole catalog, no denominator caveat: the column is NOT NULL and every title carries one of skeleton / enriched / stub.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT titles.enrichment_state AS state,
       count(*) AS titles_in_state
FROM titles
GROUP BY titles.enrichment_state
ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Owned vs catalog coverage
panels.description: media_items.available and media_items.title_id against the catalog. 'Owned titles' counts distinct matched titles, so an item with no title_id is in the unmatched row and in no other.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT 'catalog titles' AS bucket, count(*) AS rows_counted
FROM titles
UNION ALL
SELECT 'owned titles (matched)', count(DISTINCT media_items.title_id)
FROM media_items
WHERE media_items.available AND media_items.title_id IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'owned items (available)', count(*)
FROM media_items
WHERE media_items.available
UNION ALL
SELECT 'owned items (unmatched)', count(*)
FROM media_items
WHERE media_items.available AND media_items.title_id IS NULL

panels.title: Unmatched review queue depth
panels.description: media_items.title_id IS NULL, served by ix_media_items_unmatched (source_id) WHERE title_id IS NULL. This panel is a count, not a page, so list_unmatched's OFFSET cost (PRD 10, dashboard 3) does not apply to it. Deliberately uncoloured: no bar has been set for this queue, and a default threshold would render 5,500 as an alarm nobody declared.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT sources.name AS source,
       count(*) AS unmatched
FROM media_items
JOIN sources ON sources.id = media_items.source_id
WHERE media_items.title_id IS NULL
GROUP BY sources.id, sources.name
ORDER BY count(*) DESC

panels.title: Genre distribution
panels.description: GROUP BY unnest(titles.genres), which is the exact facet collapse db-and-sql.md names. A title with three genres is counted three times, so the column sum exceeds the catalog and is not a denominator.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT exploded.genre AS genre,
       count(*) AS titles_with_genre
FROM (
    SELECT unnest(titles.genres) AS genre
    FROM titles
    WHERE cardinality(titles.genres) > 0
) AS exploded
GROUP BY exploded.genre
ORDER BY count(*) DESC
LIMIT 25

panels.title: Decade distribution
panels.description: titles.year, non-null on 1,128,000 of 1,276,268 rows (2026-09-07). Bounded below at 1870, which excludes exactly one row carrying year = 1.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ((titles.year / 10) * 10)::text AS decade,
       count(*) AS titles_in_decade
FROM titles
WHERE titles.year IS NOT NULL AND titles.year >= 1870
GROUP BY (titles.year / 10) * 10
ORDER BY (titles.year / 10) * 10

panels.title: Language distribution
panels.description: ⚠️ Enriched tier only. titles.original_language is non-null on exactly 133,447 rows — the enriched count to the row — so this panel is 10.5% of the catalog and 85.0% of the owned library, not the catalog.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT titles.original_language AS language,
       count(*) AS titles_in_language
FROM titles
WHERE titles.original_language IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY titles.original_language
ORDER BY count(*) DESC
LIMIT 20

panels.title: Runtime distribution
panels.description: titles.runtime_minutes, non-null on 715,395 of 1,276,268 rows (2026-09-07). Ten-minute buckets; the 240 bucket is 240 and over.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT least((titles.runtime_minutes / 10) * 10, 240)::text AS runtime_bucket_minutes,
       count(*) AS titles_in_bucket
FROM titles
WHERE titles.runtime_minutes IS NOT NULL AND titles.runtime_minutes > 0
GROUP BY least((titles.runtime_minutes / 10) * 10, 240)
ORDER BY least((titles.runtime_minutes / 10) * 10, 240)

panels.title: Library growth per week
panels.description: media_items.added_at, with an explicit IS NOT NULL. 0 of 23,943 rows are null today, so the filter is structural rather than live — the next source to report no DateCreated would empty part of the curve without raising anything.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT date_trunc('week', media_items.added_at) AS time,
       count(*) AS items_added
FROM media_items
WHERE media_items.available
  AND media_items.added_at IS NOT NULL
  AND $__timeFilter(media_items.added_at)
GROUP BY date_trunc('week', media_items.added_at)
ORDER BY date_trunc('week', media_items.added_at)

panels.title: Quality ladder by decade
panels.description: ⚠️ The share is of probed items, never of the table. HdrFormat has no SDR member, so hdr_format IS NULL means 'SDR or never probed' — 22,239 of 23,943 rows. The denominator here is media_items.video_codec IS NOT NULL (20,857 rows on 2026-09-07); 3,021 available rows carry no container at all, 3,007 of them series-level rows with no file behind them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ((titles.year / 10) * 10)::text AS decade,
       count(*) AS probed_items,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE media_items.width >= 3840) AS uhd_items,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE media_items.width >= 3840) / count(*), 1) AS uhd_pct,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE media_items.hdr_format IS NOT NULL) AS hdr_items,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE media_items.hdr_format IS NOT NULL) / count(*), 1) AS hdr_pct,
       round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE media_items.video_codec IN ('hevc', 'av1')) / count(*), 1) AS hevc_or_av1_pct
FROM media_items
JOIN titles ON titles.id = media_items.title_id
WHERE media_items.available
  AND media_items.video_codec IS NOT NULL
  AND titles.year IS NOT NULL
  AND titles.year >= 1870
GROUP BY (titles.year / 10) * 10
ORDER BY (titles.year / 10) * 10

panels.title: Most-represented directors and actors
panels.description: ⚠️ Enriched tier only, and scoped to the owned library on purpose: credits arrive from TMDb enrichment, which is 10.5% of the catalog but 85.0% of the shelf (9,784 of 11,516 owned titles, 2026-09-07). The second figure is the one that bounds a panel drawn over the shelf. One target rather than two: two targets render as two frames behind a selector, so half the panel is a click away and is not observed by anyone reading the dashboard.

targets.rawSql:
WITH owned AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT media_items.title_id AS title_id
    FROM media_items
    WHERE media_items.available AND media_items.title_id IS NOT NULL
),
directors AS (
    SELECT people.name AS person,
           count(DISTINCT credits.title_id) AS owned_titles
    FROM credits
    JOIN owned ON owned.title_id = credits.title_id
    JOIN people ON people.id = credits.person_id
    WHERE credits.kind = 'crew' AND credits.job = 'Director'
    GROUP BY people.id, people.name
    ORDER BY count(DISTINCT credits.title_id) DESC, people.name
    LIMIT 15
),
actors AS (
    SELECT people.name AS person,
           count(DISTINCT credits.title_id) AS owned_titles
    FROM credits
    JOIN owned ON owned.title_id = credits.title_id
    JOIN people ON people.id = credits.person_id
    WHERE credits.kind = 'cast'
    GROUP BY people.id, people.name
    ORDER BY count(DISTINCT credits.title_id) DESC, people.name
    LIMIT 15
)
SELECT 'director' AS role, directors.person AS person, directors.owned_titles AS owned_titles
FROM directors
UNION ALL
SELECT 'actor', actors.person, actors.owned_titles
FROM actors
ORDER BY role DESC, owned_titles DESC, person

panels.title: Franchise completeness (the want-list)
panels.description: ⚠️ Enriched tier only. titles.collection_id arrives from TMDb enrichment (13,381 rows in a collection, 5,298 collections on 2026-09-07), so a franchise whose other entries were never enriched reads as complete. Rows are franchises with at least one owned entry and at least one missing one; 'missing' is the want-list.

targets.rawSql:
WITH owned AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT media_items.title_id AS title_id
    FROM media_items
    WHERE media_items.available
      AND media_items.title_id IS NOT NULL
      AND media_items.episode_id IS NULL
)
SELECT collections.name AS franchise,
       count(*) AS entries,
       count(owned.title_id) AS owned_entries,
       count(*) - count(owned.title_id) AS missing_entries,
       string_agg(
           titles.name || coalesce(' (' || titles.year || ')', ''),
           ', ' ORDER BY titles.year NULLS LAST, titles.name
       ) FILTER (WHERE owned.title_id IS NULL) AS missing
FROM titles
JOIN collections ON collections.id = titles.collection_id
LEFT JOIN owned ON owned.title_id = titles.id
GROUP BY collections.id, collections.name
HAVING count(owned.title_id) > 0 AND count(owned.title_id) < count(*)
ORDER BY count(*) - count(owned.title_id) DESC, collections.name
LIMIT 50
